label: The Model Spaces
notes: This chapter, printed pages 15 through 31, builds one family of reference geometries. For every real number k there is a complete, simply connected space of constant curvature k. These three model shapes, sphere, plane and hyperbolic disk, are the rulers against which every later curvature bound is measured.

label: One Construction, Three Signs
notes: Stress the uniformity: positive, zero and negative curvature are not three unrelated theories but one construction read off at three signs of k. Rescaling reduces any positive k to the unit sphere and any negative k to standard hyperbolic space, so only the sign and a scale factor ever matter.

label: Euclidean Space E^n
notes: Euclidean space is the calibration case where curvature vanishes. Walk through the standard inner-product distance and the ordinary law of cosines. Emphasize that geodesics are honest straight segments and that the diameter is infinite, since every other model is described as a curved deformation of this flat baseline.

label: The Sphere S^n
notes: On the unit sphere distance is the angle subtended at the centre, computed from the Euclidean dot product through arccosine. Geodesics are great-circle arcs. Highlight the finite diameter pi and the fact that antipodal points are joined by infinitely many minimizing geodesics, unlike the other two models.

label: Hyperbolic Space H^n
notes: Hyperbolic space lives on the upper sheet of a hyperboloid under the Lorentzian form. Distance uses the inverse hyperbolic cosine of minus the Minkowski product. Geodesics are intersections with planes through the origin. The space is unbounded, and triangles will turn out to be thinner than their Euclidean comparisons.

label: Rescaling to General k
notes: Explain the scaling dictionary. Multiplying the metric of the unit sphere or standard hyperbolic space by one over root k reproduces every nonzero curvature. So results proved for the three reference values transfer automatically, and the diameter formula pi over root k for positive k drops straight out of this rescaling.

label: The Law of Cosines
notes: Present the three cosine rules side by side. The Euclidean rule is the linear template; the spherical and hyperbolic rules replace lengths by sine or hyperbolic sine and cosine of the curvature-scaled sides. Point out that letting k tend to zero recovers the flat rule, confirming the family is continuous in k.

label: Geodesics in Each Model
notes: Compare the geodesics directly: straight lines, great-circle arcs, and hyperboloid sections. Emphasize that each model is uniquely geodesic below its diameter, so a triangle is determined by its three vertices. This unique joining is exactly what makes the models usable as comparison spaces for CAT(k) later.

label: Diameter and Curvature Sign
notes: Tie the global size of each model to the sign of k. Positive curvature closes the space up at diameter pi over root k; zero and negative curvature leave it infinite. This single number governs which comparison triangles can be built, and it reappears as the diameter constraint in the definition of CAT(k).

label: Triangle Thickness vs k
notes: This is the geometric punchline. With sides fixed, a larger curvature fattens a triangle and shrinks its angle sum below the bound on the sphere side, while negative curvature thins it and pushes the angle sum under pi. Comparison geometry will pin abstract triangles between these reference shapes.

label: Isometry Groups
notes: Each model is highly symmetric: its isometry group acts transitively on points and on frames, so the geometry looks identical everywhere and in every direction. Name the orthogonal, Euclidean and Lorentz groups. This homogeneity is why a single comparison triangle, placed anywhere, captures the whole model.

label: Why M_k^n Are the Rulers
notes: Close by stating the payoff. The model spaces are the fixed measuring instruments: a geodesic triangle in an arbitrary space is compared to a triangle with the same side lengths drawn in M_k. Curvature bounded above by k means real triangles are no fatter than their model comparisons. That comparison is the whole game.
